title: South Korea says chip investments under discussion with US amid tariff concerns
author: B
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

South Korea and the United States are discussing additional semiconductor investment as Seoul seeks clarity over Washington’s planned tariffs on imported chips, a South Korean presidential official said Friday.

The talks form part of wider bilateral negotiations and come after US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick signalled that the administration is preparing a targeted tariff policy designed to encourage chipmakers to manufacture in the United States. Seoul is assessing how the proposed duties could affect Korean companies and previously agreed investment commitments.

Under a deal reached by the countries’ presidents last year, South Korea pledged $350 billion for US manufacturing projects. The agreement says Korean semiconductor producers should receive tariff treatment no less favourable than that granted to competitors with an equal or greater volume of chip trade.

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the world’s leading memory-chip manufacturers, are central to the discussions. Both companies are strategically important to US technology firms, which need supplies of advanced memory for artificial-intelligence data centres. Any tariff structure linking duty exemptions to American production could increase pressure on them to expand their US operations, even as they invest at home.

The presidential official said issues between Seoul and Washington sometimes influence one another, either helping or complicating negotiations, but added that both sides were trying to prevent disputes from escalating.

The investment discussions underscore the difficult balance facing South Korea: preserving access to its largest technology markets, protecting domestic industrial capacity and managing an alliance increasingly shaped by trade, security and competition over critical technologies.
